description: Machine-readable evidence matrix for all optimization modules in EPIC-05 repository. See reports/epic05/research-alignment-audit-2026-08-27.md for narrative analysis.

M0.name: baseline
M0.description: gsplat default pipeline: tile_size=16, packed=True, SH degree=3, eps2d=0.1, radius_clip=0.0

evidence.forward_correctness_note: Default configuration; reference for all comparisons
evidence.backward_correctness_note: gsplat native backward kernels exist and execute (loss.backward() works)
evidence.gradient_correctness_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-01: torch.autograd.gradcheck PASS on all 5 parameter groups. Finite-difference (central, eps=1e-4/1e-5): max_abs_error=0.0 for xyz/scales/rotations/opacity, 1.03e-7 for shs (near-zero gradient artifact). Gradients identical between tile16 and tile32 within floating-point precision.
evidence.quality_layer_a_note: Reference baseline; compared against self = bit-exact
evidence.quality_layer_b_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-01: Pixel-identical renderings between tile16 and tile32 on 3 Mip-NeRF 360 scenes (bicycle 6.1M, garden 5.8M, room 1.6M) at 1080p. PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS deltas = 0.0 for all scenes. Per-pixel max error = 0.0. Quality gate: QUALITY_PASS.
evidence.performance_inference_note: tile16 reference: 15.89ms (50K) / 38.55ms (200K) / 43.65ms (400K) on A100; 20.72ms (bicycle) / 16.70ms (garden) / 7.09ms (room) on RTX 5070
evidence.performance_training_note: M0 as tile16 is used as training baseline in phase4/phase5 scripts but no dedicated training benchmark for M0 itself
evidence.training_simplified_note: Simplified training (no densification/pruning, random GT) executed for room (5000 steps) as baseline
evidence.training_full_note: Full training with densification, pruning, SH progression, real GT never executed

M1.name: tile_size
M1.description: Runtime tile size parameter in gsplat.rasterization(). Same compiled kernel binary, only grid dimensions and threads-per-block change.
M1.mechanism: CUDA grid launch parameter: threads/block = tile_size^2, blocks = ceil(W/tile_size) * ceil(H/tile_size). Same binary (cuobjdump verified: REG=40, SHARED=1024, STACK=0 for all tile sizes).

evidence.forward_correctness_note: tile16 vs tile32 bit-exact on bicycle/garden (max error=0.0); room max error=0.002481 (floating-point reduction order artifact). tile8 vs tile16 bit-exact on bicycle/garden.
evidence.backward_correctness_note: Backward executes and produces gradients for all 5 parameter groups (means, scales, rotations, opacity, shs) at both tile16 and tile32. Gradient norms at tile16 vs tile32 differ by < 5e-7 relative (floating-point reduction order).
evidence.gradient_correctness_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-01: torch.autograd.gradcheck PASS on all 5 parameter groups for both tile16 and tile32 (eps=1e-4, atol=1e-3, rtol=1e-3). Finite-difference (central, n=100, eps=1e-4/1e-5): max_abs_error=0.0 (xyz, scales, rotations, opacity), max_abs_error=1.03e-7 (shs — near-zero gradient elements). Gradients are identical between tile16 and tile32 within floating-point precision. See reports/epic05/gradient-correctness-tile-size-2026-09-01.md.
evidence.quality_layer_a_note: Pixel equivalence confirmed between tile16/tile32 and tile16/tile8 on official scenes (bicycle, garden: bit-exact; room: max 0.002 pixel diff)
evidence.quality_layer_b_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-01: Pixel-identical renderings between tile16 and tile32 on 3 Mip-NeRF 360 scenes (bicycle, garden, room) at 1080p. PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS deltas = 0.0. Per-pixel max error = 0.0. Quality gate: QUALITY_PASS across all scenes. Data: results/epic05/layer_b_quality_summary.json
evidence.performance_inference_note: A100: tile32 1.42x-3.93x faster than tile16 (50K-400K synthetic). RTX 5070: tile16 1.03x-1.53x faster than tile32 (official scenes, 1080p). Tile preference is hardware-dependent.
evidence.performance_training_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-02: room 30K full training. tile16: 150.3min, 3.33 iter/s. tile32: 94.8min, 5.27 iter/s. Speedup 1.58×. tile32 faster at all stages in v2 full-run. See phase7b_training_mechanism_analysis.md.
evidence.training_simplified_note: Room 3000-step mid training completed (tile16: 17.2min, tile32: 28.0min). Full 30K training completed (tile16: 150.3min, tile32: 94.8min). v2 full-run shows tile32 faster at every iteration. Cross-scene (bicycle, garden) BLOCKED by server.
evidence.training_full_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-02: Full 30K training on room with real GT, L1+D-SSIM, densification/pruning, SH progression. tile16: 150.3min, 29.27dB, 1,193,480 Gs. tile32: 94.8min, 29.39dB, 1,146,273 Gs. Speedup 1.58×. Cross-scene BLOCKED by server.
evidence.composability_note: tile32+dense, tile32+SH0, tile32+rclip tested for performance only (no gradient/composability gate). No meaningful interaction effects detected in performance, but gradient interactions untested.
evidence.training_with_real_gt_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-02: Full 30K training on room with real GT completed for both tile16 and tile32. See phase7_training_status_2026-09-02.md.

M2.name: packed_dense
M2.description: Packed mode skips invisible Gaussians per camera; dense mode processes all Gaussians.
M2.mechanism: Compaction kernel removes invalid camera/Gaussian pairs before rasterization. Separate CUDA projection kernel (_fully_fused_projection_packed vs _fully_fused_projection). Rasterization kernel binary identical; stride differs.

evidence.forward_correctness_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-15 (Phase 9A): Bit-exact pixel match (max_abs_diff=0.0) between packed and dense on room scene (1.6M Gs, 1080p). 2.02x forward speedup for packed (inference) due to 75% fewer SH evaluations (only 24.5% of Gaussians visible).
evidence.backward_correctness_note: Backward produces gradients for all 5 param groups in both packed and dense modes. Gradient norms between packed and dense differ by < 5.5e-7 relative (floating-point precision).
evidence.gradient_correctness_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-15 (Phase 9A): Gradient comparison on real room scene (1.6M Gs, 1080p). All 5 parameter groups show near-identical gradient norms (max_rel_diff 3.5e-6 for quats, < 8e-8 for all others). All gradients finite. No NaN/Inf in either mode.
evidence.quality_layer_a_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-15 (Phase 9A): Packed vs dense produce bit-identical pixel output (max_diff=0.0) on room at 1080p. Identical pixel output means identical GT quality.
evidence.quality_layer_b_note: Identical pixel output between packed and dense → identical GT quality against real images.
evidence.performance_inference_note: Packed 2.02x faster on room (1.6M Gs, 1080p): 9.87ms vs 19.91ms. Driven by reduced SH evaluation and tile intersection.
evidence.performance_training_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-15 (Phase 9A): 500-step training on room. Packed fwd 20.15ms vs dense 27.97ms (1.39x). But packed bwd 34.00ms vs dense 29.51ms (0.87x). Net: dense 1.18x faster overall (288s vs 339s). No E2E benefit for packed in training.
evidence.training_simplified_note: 500-step real-GT training with full pipeline (densification, pruning, SH progression). Both modes stable: no NaN/Inf, loss decreases, Gaussian trajectory nearly identical.
evidence.training_full_note: 30K full training not strictly necessary: packed=True is the DEFAULT mode used in all Phase 7 baseline training. 500-step sanity shows no divergence.
evidence.composability_note: All gates PASS except 30K full training (NOT_TESTED). M2 composability eligibility: PENDING_FULL_TRAINING per Phase 9B policy. Forward bit-exact, gradient norms match within 4e-6, training sanity PASS.
evidence.training_with_real_gt_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-15: 500-step training with real GT images on room scene. Stable loss/PSNR trajectory for both packed and dense.

M3.name: sh_degree
M3.description: Spherical harmonic degree controls color representation fidelity (0=DC only, 1=4 coeffs, 3=16 coeffs).
M3.mechanism: Number of SH coefficients per Gaussian: (degree+1)^2 * 3 values. SH0: 1 base (DC), SH1: 4 bases (DC+linear), SH3: 16 bases (full 3rd order). Rasterization, tile intersection, CUB sort are identical across all degrees.

evidence.forward_correctness_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-21: SH0/SH1/SH3 produce valid renderings on room scene (1.6M Gs, 1080p). Steady-state timing: SH0=9.25ms, SH1=9.80ms, SH3=10.51ms. Varies by <7%. Data: results/epic05/phase9b/m3_forward_quality.json. Report: reports/epic05/phase9b_m3_source_trace.md.
evidence.backward_correctness_note: spherical_harmonics_bwd_kernel executes and produces finite gradients for all param groups at SH degree=0,1,3. spherical_harmonics_bwd_kernel<40 regs> verified. Confirmed on real room scene with 1.6M Gs.
evidence.gradient_correctness_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-21: All 5 parameter groups (means, quats, scales, opacities, shs) produce finite gradients at SH0/SH1/SH3 on real room scene (1.6M Gs, 1080p). No NaN/Inf. Consistent with prior gradcheck PASS. Gradient norms vary by degree as expected (different color representation changes loss landscape).
evidence.quality_layer_a_note: SH0 vs SH3: PSNR=30.69dB, SSIM=0.939, LPIPS=0.036. SH1 vs SH3: PSNR=32.82dB, SSIM=0.960, LPIPS=0.025. This is a representation capacity trade-off, not a correctness issue. Lower SH degree = lower color fidelity = lower PSNR vs full reference.
evidence.quality_layer_b_note: Quality/performance trade-off characterized. SH0/SH1 produce recognizable high-quality renderings despite lower capacity. SH1 is closer to SH3 (ΔPSNR 2.1dB) than SH0 (ΔPSNR 3.9dB).
evidence.performance_inference_note: Forward-only inference: SH0 ≈ 0.88× SH3 (1.3ms faster). The spherical harmonics kernel has negligible cost vs rasterization.
evidence.performance_training_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-21: 500-step training. Per-iteration: SH0=41.0ms, SH1=45.0ms, SH3=61.9ms. Dominant cost is optimizer step (scales with SH param count: SH0 4.09ms vs SH3 21.69ms). Fwd/bwd nearly identical. Peak VRAM: SH0=1,651MB, SH1=1,946MB, SH3=3,172MB.
evidence.training_simplified_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-21: 500-step real-GT training with full pipeline (densification, pruning, SH progression). All 3 degrees stable: no NaN/Inf, loss decreasing, Gaussian trajectory nearly identical, converged PSNR ~30 dB for all.
evidence.training_full_note: Full 30K training would require ~20h on RTX 5070. 500-step sanity shows stable trajectories. SH3 is the default (already validated in Phase 7 30K). Not required for composability eligibility.
evidence.composability_note: All gates PASS except 30K full training (NOT_TESTED). M3 composability eligibility: PENDING_FULL_TRAINING per Phase 9B policy. Quality diff is a representation capacity trade-off, not a correctness failure.
evidence.training_with_real_gt_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-21: 500-step training with real GT images on room scene. All 3 SH degrees stable with converged PSNR ~30 dB.

M4.name: radius_clip
M4.description: Near/far clipping of projected Gaussian screen-space radius.
M4.mechanism: Filters Gaussians with projected radius below threshold

evidence.forward_correctness_note: Performance difference ±0.1%. No pixel equivalence study.
evidence.backward_correctness_note: Backward produces finite gradients for all 5 param groups across radius_clip=0.0/0.001/0.005/0.01. Rel diff vs rclip=0.0 < 3.1e-7.
evidence.gradient_correctness_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-01: Gradient comparison at rclip=0.0/0.001/0.005/0.01 on synthetic scene (50K, 1080p). All 5 param groups show near-identical gradient norms (rel_diff < 3.1e-7 vs rclip=0.0). All gradients finite.

M5.name: eps2d
M5.description: Additive epsilon to 2D covariance diagonal for numerical stability.
M5.mechanism: Adds eps to 2D covariance matrix diagonal to prevent degeneracy

evidence.forward_correctness_note: Performance difference ±0.1%. No pixel equivalence study.
evidence.backward_correctness_note: Backward produces finite gradients for all 5 param groups across eps2d=0.01/0.1/0.3/0.5. Small diff vs default expected (eps2d changes numerical path).
evidence.gradient_correctness_note: VERIFIED 2026-09-01: Gradient comparison at eps2d=0.01/0.1/0.3/0.5 on synthetic scene (50K, 1080p). All 5 param groups produce finite gradients. Grad norms vary by 2-5e-6 rel diff between values (expected: eps2d is an additive blur that affects the 2D covariance projection).

M6.name: higs_tile_size
M6.description: HiGS inference renderer tile size. Separate renderer class (GaussianInferenceRenderer) not gsplat.rasterization().
M6.mechanism: Coarse macro-tiles for sorting + fine render tiles for rasterization. Tile size controls render tile granularity.

evidence.forward_correctness_note: HiGS output compared to gsplat dense ~59 dB PSNR synthetic consistency check. Paired-reference audit showed ~0.626 dB drop attributed but gsplat dense reproduced same drop.
evidence.backward_correctness_note: HiGS is inference-only (GaussianInferenceRenderer class). No backward kernels available.
evidence.gradient_correctness_note: HiGS has no backward pass — non-differentiable. Cannot participate in training.
evidence.quality_layer_a_note: Consistency check with gsplat dense performed. Quality difference attributed to gsplat path issue, not HiGS optimization itself.
evidence.quality_layer_b_note: Paired-reference audit on official Train model with quality thresholds
evidence.performance_inference_note: HiGS significantly faster than gsplat at high Gaussian counts (P99 7.23ms vs 876ms at 200K; median ~16ms vs 1609ms at 400K).
evidence.performance_training_note: Inference-only renderer — no training mode available
evidence.composability_note: HiGS not included in interaction experiments

M7.name: higs_sh_compression
M7.description: HiGS SH coefficient compression: none (FP32), 32b (half precision), 16b (quarter precision).
M7.mechanism: FP16/FP8 packing of SH coefficients to reduce memory bandwidth

evidence.forward_correctness_note: SH32: min 64.85 dB against uncompressed HiGS. SH16: min 49.79 dB — significant quality degradation at SH16.
evidence.quality_layer_a_note: PSNR comparison against uncompressed HiGS available. SH32 safe (64.85 dB min), SH16 degraded (49.79 dB min).
evidence.quality_layer_b_note: Min PSNR numbers available from synthetic comparison
evidence.performance_inference_note: SH32 sometimes slower at 50K (decode overhead), matches uncompressed at 400K with P99 improvement. SH16 faster but quality-degraded.

M8.name: higs_auto_adapter
M8.description: Scale-aware HiGS configuration: <300K Gaussians -> tile16+SHnone; >=300K -> tile8+SH32b.
M8.mechanism: Heuristic rule based on Gaussian count threshold (300K)

evidence.forward_correctness_note: Combination of M6+M7; individual evidence applies
evidence.performance_inference_note: Auto adapter matches optimal tile for each Gaussian count range

M9.name: tc_gs
M9.description: Tensor Core matrix operations for alpha computation. Separate repository (DeepLink-org/3DGSTensorCore).
M9.mechanism: Maps conditional alpha computation to Tensor Core matrix operations (reportedly 2.18x additional speedup)

evidence.forward_correctness_note: Smoke test on RTX 5070: 4.614ms vs 6.125ms for gsplat dense (10 frames, native cameras). Within quality thresholds vs original 3DGS.
evidence.backward_correctness_note: TC-GS backward path not tested in this repository
evidence.quality_layer_a_note: Smoke test within configured paired-reference quality thresholds
evidence.performance_inference_note: ~1.33x vs gsplat dense on room scene (RTX 5070). Single scene only.
evidence.performance_training_note: Training not tested in this repository
evidence.composability_note: TC-GS not combined with other modules in this repository

phase8c.title: Phase 8C — Backward path decomposition + workload quantification
phase8c.description: Trace every backward kernel, measure workload stats, evaluate H7 hypotheses on frozen room checkpoints
phase8c.key_finding: Phase 8B backward ratios (137-234x) NOT reproducible. Fresh cold-GPU measurement shows 2.6-6.3x ratio, fully explained by 4x intersection count. Phase 8B extreme ratios caused by GPU thermal throttling.

phase8d.title: Phase 8D — Forward path decomposition + superlinear scaling analysis
phase8d.description: Complete forward kernel trace (8 kernels/CUB calls), identify which kernels are tile_size-dependent, quantify workload metrics (M1-M8), evaluate forward superlinear scaling hypotheses
phase8d.key_finding: tile16 forward superlinear scaling (1.33x Gs count → 9.64x runtime) is not explained by total Gaussian count, intersection count, or visible Gaussian count. The most complete explanation is H7: Rasterization Kernel Batch Overhead — tile16 has 15.5x more batch-launch operations (571K-694K vs 37K-45K) due to 4x smaller block size (256 vs 1024). Per-intersection cost increases 7.96x from iter5000→iter30000. Per-kernel timing BLOCKED (needs CUDA event wrappers). Nsight Compute profiling BLOCKED (WDDM).
